title: A fixed three-dimensional Krylov compression lowers the Wick variational coefficient strictly beyond minus one

three_dimensional_ritz.basis: Use the orthonormal Krylov basis e0=1, e1=X_N=V_N/sigma_N and e2=Y_N from K1488
three_dimensional_ritz.multiplication_matrix: Compression of X_N is [[0,1,0],[1,mu_N,tau_N],[0,tau_N,eta_N]], with mu_N=E(X_N^3), tau_N>=1 and eta_N=E(X_N Y_N^2)
three_dimensional_ritz.moment_bounds: K1483 gives 0<=mu_N<=72S_N/sigma_N=o(1). Nelson hypercontractivity gives ||X_N||_4<=9 and ||Y_N||_4<=81, hence |eta_N|<=||Y_N||_4^2<=6561
three_dimensional_ritz.fixed_trial: For t=1/6562 use the coefficient vector (1,-1,t). Once mu_N<=1/(2*6562), its normalized X_N Rayleigh quotient is at most -1-c_star with c_star=1/39372
three_dimensional_ritz.free_cost: The trial has Wiener degree at most eight, so its normalized H0 form value is at most 8 omega_max(N)=O(N)
three_dimensional_ritz.ground_energy_upper: For every fixed g>0 and all sufficiently large N, E_N<=6gC_N^2-(1+c_star)g sigma_N+O(N), c_star=1/39372
three_dimensional_ritz.strict_consequence: The coefficient -1 from the vacuum--fourth-chaos compression is not the leading full variational coefficient; at least one higher-chaos direction lowers it by a cutoff-independent fraction
three_dimensional_ritz.ceiling: The universal constant is deliberately crude. This remains an upper bound and does not determine the true correction scale, a matching lower bound, ground-state localization or a continuum limit
